Notebook.Title: Htop: Live Monitoring From Another Thread

Section.Title: Welcome
Section.Paragraph: All three cells below share Scope="htop" and run as one program against one world. Scene 2 spawns a real background Thread that watches the same World the other scenes touch — this is the one notebook where Stop's best-effort nature matters most: the monitor thread waits on a signal each frame, so an interrupt there actually has a place to take effect.

Section.Title: Scene 1: Which Exporters Are Wired Up?
Section.Paragraph: IMetricsExporter is an ordinary interface that also implements IAddon — world.GetAddon<IMetricsExporter>() finds any addon implementing it, and GetAddons<T>() finds all of them, which is how a world can host several independent exporters side by side.

Section.Title: Scene 2: htop Watches the Kernel From Another Thread
Section.Paragraph: SubWorldAddon hands out a second World (the "monitor" world) that mirrors entities out of the first via ExtractSystemBase/SnapshotExtractSystem, so a background thread can read a consistent snapshot without racing the kernel world's own tick. ExtractChannel<T> is the thread-safe mailbox alerts travel through in the other direction.

Section.Title: Scene 3: Chaos Monkey
Section.Paragraph: query.ForEachOnParallel fans a query out across worker threads; collecting the entities to destroy into a ConcurrentStack<Entity> first (rather than calling Destroy() from inside the parallel callback) keeps the actual structural change single-threaded and safe.
